First, recall that:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 1}f(t) & =({lim}_{t\to 1}\frac{4+t}{5})\,i+({lim}_{t\to 1}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(t-1)}{{t}^{2}-1})\,j+({lim}_{t\to 1}\sqrt{9t})\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the limits one-by-one.

- For the first component, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 1}\frac{4+t}{5} & =\frac{4+1}{5}=1\end{aligned}
$$

- The second component can be found using a special limit:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 1}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(t-1)}{{t}^{2}-1} & ={lim}_{t\to 1}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(t-1)}{(t-1)(t+1)} \\  & =({lim}_{t\to 1}\frac{1}{t+1})\cdot ({lim}_{t\to 1}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(t-1)}{t-1}) \\  & =(\frac{1}{1+1})\cdot 1 \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

- For the third component, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 1}\sqrt{9t} & =\sqrt{9(1)}=3\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, ${lim}_{t\to 1}f(t)=i+\frac{1}{2}\,j+3\,k.$

Finally, the limit of $‖f(t)‖$ as $t$ approaches $1$ is:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 1}‖f(t)‖ & =‖{lim}_{t\to 1}f(t)‖ \\  & =‖i+\frac{1}{2}\,j+3\,k‖ \\  & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{(\frac{1}{2})}^{2}+{3}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+\frac{1}{4}+9} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{41}{4}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{41}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$
